Sam Reynolds: FYI, Enterprise customer reported function-call failures when using streaming responses through their edge proxy. They see a JSON parse error from our tool router. Attaching their minimal repro below.

Maria Gonzales: Can you paste the exact error they see?

Sam Reynolds: "Function call failed: unexpected end of JSON input" from our runtime logs. Happens consistently for payloads ~2.1KB+ when client streams via chunked transfer. Says it worked if they disable streaming.

Jin Park: Do we have any logs from the proxy side? chunk sizes?

Sam Reynolds: They sent a small capture (sanitized). Looks like an SSE stream with the last event cutting off mid-object.

Sam Reynolds: ```
data: {\"tool\":\"billingQuery\", \"args\":{\"invoice_id\":\"inv_ABC12345\", \"filters\":{\"period\":\"2025-11\", \"include_credits\":true}}}  

data: {\"tool\":\"billingQuery\", \"args\":{\"invoice_id\":\"inv_ABC12346\", \"filters\":{\"period\":\"2025-11\", \"include_credits\":true}}

data: {\"tool\":\"billingQuery\", \"args\":{\"invoice_id\":\"inv_ABC47\", \"filters\":{\"period\":\"2025-11\", \"include_credits\":true}}
```

Sam Reynolds: Note the final event above is missing the closing braces (truncated). Customer asserts this arrives that way from their load balancer.

Lee Chen: What transport? Websockets, SSE, or HTTP chunked?

Sam Reynolds: They use server-sent events (text/event-stream) proxied through an internal HTTP/1.1 edge that does chunked transfer encoding. They say nginx + custom TCP proxy.

Maria Gonzales: Do we validate tool args on the streaming receive path, or only once the event is complete?

Jin Park: We parse streaming tokens as they arrive and buffer until we see the end of an SSE data field (blank line between events). If an event never ends (truncated) our parser currently attempts a best-effort JSON.parse once the 'data' terminator arrives. If terminator missing, it will eventually time out and error.

Sam Reynolds: Customer sees immediate parse error (no timeout) — suggests we attempted parse on a partial buffer. Their proxy reportedly coalesces chunk boundaries weirdly (some chunks end with CR, others start mid-utf8 multibyte).

Maria Gonzales: Could be a CRLF vs LF normalization issue that removes the blank line between events, making two events merge and produce malformed JSON. Any examples of chunk boundaries?

Sam Reynolds: They provided raw TCP capture (sanitized). I'll paste an excerpt where chunk split occurs.

Sam Reynolds: ```
...
0x0000: 64 61 74 61 3a 20 7b 22 74 6f 6f 6c 22 3a 22 62 69 6c 6c 69 6e 67 51 75 65 72 79 22 2c 20 22 61 72 67 73 22 3a 7b 22 69 6e 76 6f 69 63 65 5f 69 64 22 3a 22 69 6e 76 5f 41 42 43 31 32 33 34 35 22 2c 20 22 66 69 6c 74 65 72 73 22 3a 7b 22 70 65 72 69 6f 64 22 3a 22 32 30 32 35 2d 31 31 22 2c 20 22 69 6e 63 6c 75 64 65 5f 63 72 65 64 69 74 73 22 3a 74 72 75 65 7d 7d 7d 0d 0a
...
0x0100: 64 61 74 61 3a 20 7b 22 74 6f 6f 6c 22 3a 22 62 69 6c 6c 69 6e 67 51 75 65 72 79 22 2c 20 22 61 72 67 73 22 3a 7b 22 69 6e 76 6f 69 63 65 5f 69 64 22 3a 22 69 6e 76 5f 41 42 43 31 32 33 34 36 22 2c 20 22 66 69 6c 74 65 72 73 22 3a 7b 22 70 65 72 69 6f 64 22 3a 22 32 30 32 35 2d 31 31 22 2c 20
0x0180: 22 69 6e 63 6c 75 64 65 5f 63 72 65 64 69 74 73 22 3a 74 72 75 65 7d 7d 7d 0d 0a
...
0x0200: 64 61 74 61 3a 20 7b 22 74 6f 6f 6c 22 3a 22 62 69 6c 6c 69 6e 67 51 75 65 72 79 22 2c 20 22 61 72 67 73 22 3a 7b 22 69 6e 76 6f 69 63 65 5f 69 64 22 3a 22 69 6e 76 5f 41 42 43 34 37 22 2c 20 22 66 69 6c 74 65 72 73 22 3a 7b 22 70 65 72 69 6f 64 22 3a 22 32 30 32 35 2d 31 31 22 2c 20 22 69 6e 63 6c 75 64 65 5f 63 72 65 64 69 74 73 22 3a 74 72 75 65 7d 7d 7b
```

Sam Reynolds: See final bytes end with 7b ('{') instead of 7d ('}') — truncated.

Jin Park: OK, two hypothesis: (1) Edge proxy is truncating last chunk due to max header/body size or premature connection close; (2) Our streaming parser treats certain line endings as event terminator and tries parse early if it sees a 

Maria Gonzales: Repro risk high. Customer is on Dedicated plan; this is blocking production. We should escalate to eng-runtime and ask for a defensive parser change and a quick mitigation in the gateway.

Lee Chen: Quick mitigation options: (A) treat any `data:` event as opaque until we see a blank line delimiter, do not attempt JSON.parse on partial buffers; (B) add heuristics to detect unbalanced braces and delay parse; (C) fallback to buffering entire SSE event plus a small post-read timeout.

Sam Reynolds: Customer asked if we can accept a header hint like `x-redwood-sse-buffer: full` to force gateway to buffer per-event. They can toggle on their side but want server-side fix.

Jin Park: For immediate support I can add a temporary gate in the gateway to avoid parse attempts before a clear event boundary. Low risk change. I'll open a canary PR and test with the customer's capture.

Maria Gonzales: Also ask customer for their nginx config (proxy_buffering, chunk_size) and whether they run HTTP/2 between proxies (which can change framing).

Sam Reynolds: I'll request configs and ask them to reproduce with `curl --no-buffer` and `--http1.1` to mimic chunked streaming.

SupportBot: Incident created: INC-2026-1789 assigned to eng-runtime (Jin Park). Priority: P1 for Dedicated customer.

Lee Chen: Note: add unit tests for multibyte UTF-8 boundaries + chunk splits. We hit this before with other event sources.

Jin Park: I'll post a follow-up with a link to the PR and a small local repro harness in ~2 hours.

Sam Reynolds: Thanks team. Customer on-call wants frequent updates — I'll keep them looped in. :thumbsup:
